question: Can a simple temporal relevance component (e.g., exponential decay based solely on elapsed time) effectively handle non-uniform decay across legal domains, or is domain-adaptive weighting necessary to capture varying decay rates?
description: The non-uniform decay observed in legal statutes (stable criminal procedure vs degrading civil law) suggests that a one-size-fits-all temporal weight may be suboptimal. We need to investigate whether adaptive weighting schemes (e.g., based on document type or volatility) are required.
rationale: Answering this uncertainty affects the technical validity and potential effectiveness of the proposed framework.
